llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and network behavior align with its stated purpose as a local-first guard that optionally registers an agent with openguardrails.com; activation writes a local API key and enables cloud-assessed checks — verify provenance before activating.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included files and runtime instructions. The skill implements local detection and an optional cloud activation that registers the agent with openguardrails.com; it does not request unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts are explicit about actions: local protections are immediate after install, and running activate.mjs performs a single registration POST and writes credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json. The project warns that only sanitized metadata (not message content) is sent after activation. This is within scope, but activation performs network I/O and writes a local credential file — the user should confirm they trust the remote endpoint before completing activation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec). Installation steps call the OpenClaw plugin installer and reference the npm package @openguardrails/moltguard; that's reasonable, but users are rightly instructed to verify the npm tarball against the GitHub source before running installation/activation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested by the skill. The only persistent artifact is a credentials.json file in ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails containing an API key/agentId/claimUrl created by activation — this is proportionate to the described cloud-registration feature.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or system-wide privileges. It writes its own credential file under the user's home (~/.openclaw/...), which is expected for a plugin that optionally registers with a cloud service. The skill is allowed to be invoked autonomously (platform default); that by itself is not an anomaly but users should be aware activation expands remote visibility.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: local protections are active immediately and activation registers the agent with openguardrails.com and writes an API key to ~/.openclaw/credentials/openguardrails/credentials.json. Before activating: 1) verify provenance by running npm pack and diffing the tarball against the GitHub repo as suggested in SKILL.md; 2) inspect scripts/activate.mjs and scripts/status.mjs yourself (they are short and readable); 3) if you need high assurance, monitor the registration network call with tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch to confirm only the expected metadata is sent; 4) if you later distrust the service, delete the credentials file and revoke the key via the portal. If you do not want any outbound calls or a cloud-stored API key, skip activation — local protections remain functional without it.
